questions.question_text: A 6 ohm resistor is connected across 12 V. What current flows through it?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law, I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two resistors of 3 ohm and 6 ohm are in series across 18 V. What is the circuit current?
questions.explanation: Series resistance is 3 + 6 = 9 ohm; I = 18/9 = 2 A.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 4 ohm and 12 ohm resistor are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel branches, 1/R = 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3, so R = 3 ohm.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A wire is stretched to twice its original length without changing its volume. Assuming resistivity stays constant, how does its resistance change?
questions.option_d: It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: At constant volume, doubling length halves area; R = rho L/A therefore increases by a factor of four.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 60 W lamp is used at its rated voltage for 2 hours. How much electrical energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Energy = 0.060 kW x 2 h = 0.12 kWh.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 1000 W heater operates for 3 minutes. How much energy does it consume?
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two identical lamps are connected in parallel to an ideal constant-voltage source. If one lamp is removed, what happens to the other?
questions.option_b: It becomes a series circuit with infinite resistance
questions.option_c: Its voltage and brightness remain approximately unchanged
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch remains across the source, so removing a separate branch does not interrupt the other.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why are domestic appliances generally connected in parallel rather than in series?
questions.option_a: Parallel wiring forces identical current through every appliance
questions.option_b: A parallel circuit uses no electrical energy
questions.option_c: Series wiring would give each appliance the full supply voltage
questions.option_d: Each appliance receives the supply voltage and can operate independently
questions.explanation: Parallel connection supplies each appliance across the mains and permits independent switching.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fuse is correctly placed in which conductor of a household circuit?
questions.explanation: A fuse in the live wire disconnects the appliance from the live supply when it melts.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why should a fuse wire have a relatively low melting point?
questions.option_a: It should prevent the appliance from receiving voltage
questions.option_b: Excess current should heat and melt it before wiring overheats
questions.option_c: It should remain a permanent short circuit
questions.option_d: It must increase current during overload
questions.explanation: Joule heating under excessive current melts the fuse element and opens the circuit.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 2 kW appliance is rated at 200 V. What current does it draw at its rated voltage?
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An appliance is marked 1.5 kW, 250 V. What is its approximate operating resistance at the rating?
questions.explanation: R = V^2/P = 250^2/1500, approximately 41.7 ohm.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 5 ohm resistor carries 3 A for 10 s. How much heat is produced?
questions.explanation: Joule's law gives H = I^2Rt = 9 x 5 x 10 = 450 J.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two bulbs rated 100 W and 60 W at the same voltage are compared. Which has the lower resistance?
questions.option_a: Their ratings reveal no relation to resistance
questions.explanation: At a fixed voltage R = V^2/P, so greater power corresponds to lower resistance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A current of 0.8 A flows for 5 minutes. How much charge passes a point in the circuit?
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A metallic conductor is heated while its dimensions stay nearly fixed. What usually happens to its resistance?
questions.option_b: It decreases to half in every case
questions.explanation: In metals, increased lattice vibration with temperature generally impedes electron motion and raises resistance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change will increase the resistance of a uniform wire, with material and temperature unchanged?
questions.option_d: Replace it with a thicker wire of the same material and length
questions.explanation: R = rho L/A: resistance increases with length and decreases with area.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A voltmeter is connected to measure the potential difference across a resistor. How should it be connected?
questions.option_a: Between the live and earth wires in every test
questions.option_d: In series with the battery only
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures the potential difference between two terminals and is connected in parallel.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is an ideal ammeter designed to have very low resistance?
questions.option_a: To provide a large parallel bypass
questions.option_c: To cause negligible change to the current when connected in series
questions.option_d: To stop all current in the circuit
questions.explanation: An ammeter is placed in series; low resistance minimizes its effect on circuit current.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A short circuit in household wiring can cause dangerous heating mainly because
questions.option_a: the supply voltage instantly becomes zero
questions.option_c: the earth wire produces unlimited energy
questions.option_d: the circuit resistance becomes very small and current rises sharply
questions.explanation: With nearly unchanged supply voltage, very low resistance permits a large current and strong heating.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
